description.narrative: With 91 labs supporting 115 countries across the globe, the project seeks to tackle the complexity of development by introducing new protocols, backed by evidence and practice, testing and dissemination of solutions within and across countries.

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

Results attained under Output 1 and its targets: - Five (5) new data sources were used at Country Office level. Crowdsourcing, citizens data, Ethnography, Collective Intelligence and GIS -Five (5) Diversity of different data sources were used. Crowdsourcing, citizens data, Ethnography, Collective Intelligence and GIS - Fifty eight (58) sustainable development solutions were identified and documented - Three (3) varieties of innovation methods were used to test and iterate over the different hypotheses Codesigned with Ministry of Trade designed platforms that are not only facilitating export trade, but also support market intelligence to facilitate B2B exchanges as well as connections between Ugandan MSMEs and counterparts in other countries. A beta version of this platform can be accessed on this link https://undp-b2b.doctracker.co/, Scaled and handed over the Mulago Hospital Kitchen which was transformed from using biomass to electricity as an experiment to test the affordability and efficiency of electricity as an alternative cooking solution to biomass. This has so far fed and improved the nutrition of over 900 babies and their mothers from Jan-Nov 2022. And utilized the Accelerator Lab approach to deliver the Digitalization, Innovation and Smart Cities Programme. The programme delivery was 100% by December 2022.
Results attained under Output 2 and its targets: - Eight (8) blogs, two (2) videos, and twenty five (25) other (substantial) media posts as learnings to the Accelerator Lab Network shares with a public audience (outside of UNDP) - Two (2) lab insights, process or products were taken up by government entities. One is the handover of the converted Mulago Hospital Kitchen from biomass to electricity. This led to policy change where the Electricity Regulatory Authority (ERA) reduced the electricity tariff rate from UGX 556 per Kwh to UGX 451.4per Kwh for large institutions in Uganda. The Second one is the MSME B2B online market intelligence platform, which connects traders online and be able to export. This we are codesigning it with Ministry of Trade, Cooperatives and Industry. - 15% of partners and government increased their take up of the innovation methods included in the Accelerator Lab Network suite. The designing of the several policies building on the work that we initially did. Like the E-Commerce Policy, we are working with Ministry of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives, working with Ministry of ICT and National Guidance to codesign the National Long-term Digital Transformation Roadmap with aspects of developing Big Data utilization strategy. Working with ministry of trade to map start-ups and designing a Startup policy. - 45% Proportion of UNDP Country Office programming was influenced by the Accelerator Lab Network’s work and methodologies. This was mainly through the supporting the implementation of the Digitalization Innovation and Smart Cities (DISC) Programme and handing over a successful experiment to the Nature, Climate, and Energy Resilience (NCER) Team. Acc Lab handed over the Natural Resources Information System (NARIS), which is going to be scaled to also add wetlands, yet it was initially designed to monitor forests in a bid to provide data on the forest cover in Uganda.
Results attained under Output 3 and its targets: • Each lab member interacted more than once a week with another lab, a partner, and the global team tracking the size and density of the network effects among the Accelerator Labs using the different platforms like WhatsApp, Zoom weekly global call, meetings with different partner’s e.t.c. • 10% of information shared on different platforms showed new models, approaches, and insights documented and disseminated throughout the network. • 5% monthly increase in Twitter and LinkedIn followers was recorded. 2000+ impressions on Twitter. 200 views per month for blogs were recorded as tracking the engagement of the broader Development ecosystem with published learnings from the Accelerator Lab Network. • 7% of the conversation was influenced by the Accelerator Lab Network to track the amount of influence, learnings and methods that the Accelerator Lab Network had on the discourse of the broader Development ecosystem
